verses.text: We who are strong should carry the struggles of those whose faith is still growing, instead of only pleasing ourselves.
Each of us should look out for our neighbor’s good and help them grow stronger.
Even Christ didn’t live to please himself. Scripture says, “The insults aimed at you landed on me.”
Everything written long ago was written to teach us, so Scripture’s endurance and encouragement could keep our hope alive.
May the God who gives endurance and encouragement help you live in harmony with one another, following Christ Jesus,
so together, with one voice, you can praise the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ.
So welcome each other in, just as Christ welcomed you, and let that bring glory to God.
I’m telling you, Christ became a servant to the circumcised to show God’s faithfulness and confirm the promises made to the ancestors,
and so the Gentiles could praise God for his mercy. Scripture says, “That’s why I’ll praise you among the Gentiles and sing to your name.”
Again it says, “Celebrate, Gentiles, with God’s people!”
And again: “Praise the Lord, all you Gentiles; let every people group praise him!”
Isaiah says too, “Jesse’s root will rise up to rule the Gentiles, and the Gentiles will put their hope in him.”
May the God of hope fill you with all joy and peace as you trust him, so the Holy Spirit’s power makes your hope overflow. 🌊
My family, I’m convinced you’re already full of goodness and knowledge, and able to guide one another.
Still, I’ve written to you pretty boldly on some points, just to refresh your memory. God gave me this grace
to serve Christ Jesus among the Gentiles, like a priest serving God’s Good News, so the Gentiles can be an offering God accepts, made holy by the Holy Spirit.
So when I talk about God’s work, I can take pride in what Christ Jesus has done through me.
I won’t claim credit for anything except what Christ has done through me to bring the Gentiles to obey God—in what I’ve said and done,
through powerful signs and wonders, by God’s Spirit. From Jerusalem all the way around to Illyricum, I’ve fully shared Christ’s Good News.
I’ve made it my goal to preach where Christ hasn’t been named yet, so I wouldn’t build on someone else’s foundation.
As Scripture says, “Those who never heard about him will see, and those who never got the news will understand.”
That’s why I’ve been blocked so many times from coming to you.
But now I’ve finished my work in these regions. For years I’ve been wanting to visit you,
and I hope to see you on my way to Spain. I’m hoping to enjoy your company for a while and have you help me on my journey.
Right now, though, I’m heading to Jerusalem to serve God’s people there.
The believers in Macedonia and Achaia were glad to collect a gift for the poor believers in Jerusalem.
They were glad to do it—and they do owe them. Since the Gentiles shared in the Jews’ spiritual blessings, they should also serve them with material support.
Once I deliver this gift and make sure they receive it, I’ll head to Spain by way of your city.
I know that when I come, I’ll bring the full blessing of Christ’s Good News.
Family, by our Lord Jesus Christ and the Spirit’s love, I’m asking you: wrestle with me in prayer to God for me.
Pray I’ll be rescued from the people in Judea who refuse to believe, and that the service I’m bringing to Jerusalem will be welcomed by God’s people there.
Then, if God wills, I can come to you with joy and we can get some rest together.
May the God of peace be with all of you. Amen.
